title: A Lean formalization of smooth strongly convex interpolation in the real-valued setting
contribution_type: complete Lean formalization of an established interpolation theorem
claim: Necessary and sufficient finite-data smooth strongly convex interpolation in the platform's real-valued function class.

mathematical_scope.data: Every finite index type, including empty data.
mathematical_scope.parameters: 0 <= mu < L <= infinity; exact platform NNReal/ENNReal conventions.

predecessor_credit: Adrien B. Taylor, Julien M. Hendrickx and François Glineur: interpolation theorem and constructions, arXiv1502.05666v6 pp.7–10 inspected. N. Z. Shor: source of shared subgradient interface. mikedeng1: platform formulation/definitions; Shuze Chen: prior review. Earlier accepted queelius convex interpolation proof is included, with locally proved strong/smooth construction and new formalized necessity bridge. Alexander Richard Towell directed; OpenAI Codex developed and verified the Lean formalization using Mathlib Hahn–Banach, Riesz representation, calculus and asymptotics. No mathematical novelty or independent human review claim.
ai_assistance: Codex developed the Lean proof, verified, submitted, and archived it. Codex also prepared this archival packet.

public_disclosure.scope: Complete proof and explanation submitted as queelius, later accepted.

upstream_acceptance.meaning: Platform proof acceptance; independently reproduced locally. No independent human review is inferred.

limitations: Established theorem; no new mathematical interpolation theorem or exhaustive novelty assessment claimed.
Exact platform real-valued function class; not every extended-real convention in the paper.
Pinned Lean and third-party compiled libraries are trusted; no bootstrap verification.
Separate platform curvature, conjugacy and later SDP milestones remain outside this completed target.
